questions.title: Space-Separated List Parser
questions.objective: Read space-separated integers, double each element, and print space-separated.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Programs often receive a list of numbers on one line, separated by spaces. Python's split() breaks such a line into pieces, and int() turns each piece into a number.
• Read one line of input that contains integers separated by single spaces
• Build a list of the integers
• Make a new list where every number is doubled (multiplied by 2)
• Print the doubled numbers on one line, separated by single spaces

Example: for the input 1 2 3, the output is 2 4 6.

Given the line of integers, print the doubled list.
questions.input_format: A single line containing integers separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: the doubled integers in the same order, separated by single spaces.
hints: input().split() gives a list of strings, one for each number.
Use a list comprehension: [int(x) * 2 for x in parts].
Join the results with ' '.join(...), but convert each number to str first.
questions.reference_solution:
parts = input().split()

doubled = [int(x) * 2 for x in parts]

print(" ".join(str(x) for x in doubled))

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing integers separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: the doubled integers in the same order, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: In-Place List Reversal
questions.objective: Reverse a list in-place without using [::-1] or list.reverse(), then print it.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read a list of integers, reverse the list in place, and print it.
• "In place" means you change the list itself by swapping its items. Do not build a new list
• Do not use nums[::-1], nums.reverse() or reversed()
• Use two positions: one at the start and one at the end. Swap the two items, then move both positions toward the middle
• Stop when the two positions meet or cross
• Print the reversed list on one line, separated by spaces

Example: for the input 1 2 3 4 the output is 4 3 2 1.

Given a list of integers, print it reversed.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: the reversed list, separated by single spaces.
hints: Start with left = 0 and right = len(nums) - 1.
Python can swap two items in one line: nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left].
Loop while left < right, then add 1 to left and subtract 1 from right. Print with ' '.join(str(x) for x in nums).
questions.reference_solution:
nums = [int(x) for x in input().split()]

left = 0
right = len(nums) - 1

while left < right:
    nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left]
    left += 1
    right -= 1

print(" ".join(str(x) for x in nums))

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: the reversed list, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Remove Duplicate Elements
questions.objective: Remove duplicates while strictly maintaining first-appearance order.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read a list of integers and print it with the duplicates removed.
• Keep only the FIRST time each value appears
• The order of the kept values must be the same as their order in the input
• Do not use set(nums) to build the answer directly: a set does not keep the order

Example: for the input 3 1 3 2 1 the output is 3 1 2.

Given a list of integers, print the list without duplicates.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: the values without repeats, in first-appearance order, separated by single spaces.
hints: Build the result list one item at a time while looping over nums.
Keep a set called seen with the values you have already added.
Only append x to the result when x is not in seen, then add x to seen.
questions.reference_solution:
nums = [int(x) for x in input().split()]

seen = set()
result = []

for x in nums:
    if x not in seen:
        seen.add(x)
        result.append(x)

print(" ".join(str(x) for x in result))

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: the values without repeats, in first-appearance order, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Second Largest Distinct Value
questions.objective: Identify the second largest distinct integer in a list in single pass O(N).
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read a list of integers and print the second largest DISTINCT value.
• Distinct means equal values count only once. In 5 5 3 the largest is 5 and the second largest is 3
• Go through the list only once. Do not sort it
• If there is no second distinct value (for example all values are equal), print None

Examples: for 4 1 7 7 3 the output is 4. For 5 5 5 the output is None.

Given a list of integers, print the second largest distinct value.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: the second largest distinct value, or None if it does not exist.
hints: Keep two variables: largest and second, both starting as None.
When x is bigger than largest, the old largest becomes second and x becomes largest.
When x is smaller than largest but bigger than second (or second is None), x becomes second. Skip x when it equals largest. print(second) prints None by itself.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: the second largest distinct value, or None if it does not exist.

questions.title: Element Frequency Counter
questions.objective: Count occurrences of an item in a list without importing collections.Counter.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read a list of integers and a target value t, and print how many times t appears in the list.
• Do not use nums.count(t)
• Do not import anything (for example collections.Counter)
• Go through the list with a loop and count the matches yourself

Examples: for the list 1 2 1 3 1 and t = 1 the output is 3. For the list 4 5 and t = 9 the output is 0.

Given the list and t, print the count.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the integers of the list, separated by single spaces.
Line 2: the integer t to count.
questions.output_format: One integer: the number of times t appears in the list.
questions.constraints:
1 <= number of integers <= 10^5
-10^9 <= each integer, t <= 10^9
hints: Start a counter at 0.
Loop with for x in nums.
Add 1 to the counter every time x == t.
questions.reference_solution:
nums = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
t = int(input())

count = 0

for x in nums:
    if x == t:
        count += 1

print(count)

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: the integers of the list, separated by single spaces.
Line 2: the integer t to count.
extra_fields.output_format: One integer: the number of times t appears in the list.

questions.title: Aliasing vs Deep Copy Trap
questions.objective: Demonstrate modifying inner list via shallow copy vs deep copy.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A shallow copy (data.copy() or data[:]) makes a new outer list, but the inner lists are SHARED with the original. A deep copy (copy.deepcopy(data)) copies the inner lists too.

Read a 2D list called data, then do these steps in order:
• shallow = a shallow copy of data (use data.copy())
• deep = a deep copy of data (use copy.deepcopy(data); you may import copy)
• Append -1 to shallow[0]
• Append -2 to deep[0]
• Print data, shallow and deep, each on its own line, with a label

Because shallow[0] and data[0] are the same inner list, data also gets the -1. The deep copy is fully separate, so only deep gets the -2.

Example: for the rows 1 2 and 3 the output is:
data: [[1, 2, -1], [3]]
shallow: [[1, 2, -1], [3]]
deep: [[1, 2, -2], [3]]

Given the rows of data, print the three lists.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the number of rows R.
Next R lines: the integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format:
Three lines:
data: <data as a Python list>
shallow: <shallow as a Python list>
deep: <deep as a Python list>
questions.constraints:
1 <= R <= 50
1 <= number of integers in a row <= 50
-10^9 <= each integer <= 10^9
hints: Build data with a loop: data.append([int(x) for x in input().split()]) for each of the R rows.
import copy at the top. data.copy() only copies the outer list, but copy.deepcopy(data) copies every level.
Print a list directly to get the Python format: print('data:', data).
questions.reference_solution:
import copy

rows = int(input())
data = []
for _ in range(rows):
    data.append([int(x) for x in input().split()])

shallow = data.copy()
deep = copy.deepcopy(data)

shallow[0].append(-1)   # also changes data[0]: the inner list is shared
deep[0].append(-2)      # changes only the deep copy

print("data:", data)
print("shallow:", shallow)
print("deep:", deep)

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: the number of rows R.
Next R lines: the integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format:
Three lines:
data: <data as a Python list>
shallow: <shallow as a Python list>
deep: <deep as a Python list>

questions.title: Rotate List by K Steps
questions.objective: Rotate list right by K steps in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space, then print it.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read a list of integers and a number k, rotate the list to the right by k steps in place, and print it.
• Rotating right by 1 step moves the last item to the front: 1 2 3 4 becomes 4 1 2 3
• k can be bigger than the length of the list. Rotating a list of length n by n steps gives the same list, so use k % n
• Change the list itself and use only O(1) extra space: do not build a new list with slicing or concatenation

Trick: reverse the whole list, then reverse the first k items, then reverse the remaining items. Each reversal swaps items from both ends toward the middle.

Example: for the list 1 2 3 4 5 and k = 2 the output is 4 5 1 2 3.

Given the list and k, print the rotated list.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the integers of the list, separated by single spaces.
Line 2: the number of steps k.
questions.output_format: One line: the rotated list, separated by single spaces.
questions.constraints:
1 <= number of integers <= 10^5
0 <= k <= 10^9
-10^9 <= each integer <= 10^9
hints: Set k = k % len(nums) first.
One reversal of the part from left to right: while left < right, swap nums[left] and nums[right], then move both inward.
Do three reversals: the whole list (0 to n - 1), then 0 to k - 1, then k to n - 1.
questions.reference_solution:
nums = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
k = int(input())

n = len(nums)
k = k % n

# Reverse the whole list: [1,2,3,4,5] -> [5,4,3,2,1]
left, right = 0, n - 1
while left < right:
    nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left]
    left += 1
    right -= 1

# Reverse the first k items: -> [4,5,3,2,1]
left, right = 0, k - 1
while left < right:
    nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left]
    left += 1
    right -= 1

# Reverse the rest: -> [4,5,1,2,3]
left, right = k, n - 1
while left < right:
    nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left]
    left += 1
    right -= 1

print(" ".join(str(x) for x in nums))

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: the integers of the list, separated by single spaces.
Line 2: the number of steps k.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: the rotated list, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Stable Evens/Odds Partition
questions.objective: Reorder list so evens precede odds while preserving relative order.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read a list of integers and print it reordered so that all the even numbers come first and all the odd numbers come after them.
• Keep the original order inside each group. This is called a stable partition
• 0 is even. Negative numbers follow the same rule: -4 is even and -3 is odd

Example: for the input 3 8 5 2 7 4 the output is 8 2 4 3 5 7.

Given a list of integers, print the partitioned list.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: the even numbers in their original order, followed by the odd numbers in their original order, separated by single spaces.
hints: A number x is even when x % 2 == 0. In Python this also works for negative numbers.
Make two lists, evens and odds, and append each number to the right one.
Print evens + odds joined with spaces.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the integers, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: the even numbers in their original order, followed by the odd numbers in their original order, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Matrix Transpose
questions.objective: Transpose an N x M matrix into an M x N matrix.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A matrix is stored in Python as a list of rows, where each row is a list. The transpose of a matrix turns its rows into columns: the item at row i, column j moves to row j, column i.

Read an N x M matrix and print its transpose, which is an M x N matrix.
• Do not use zip(*matrix) or any library; build the result with loops
• Print the result row by row: each row on its own line, items separated by spaces

Example: for the 2 x 3 matrix
1 2 3
4 5 6
the output is
1 4
2 5
3 6

Given a matrix, print its transpose.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and M (the number of rows and columns).
Next N lines: the M integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: M lines: the rows of the transposed matrix, each with N integers separated by single spaces.
hints: Row j of the result is [matrix[i][j] for i in range(n)].
Build the result with a loop over j in range(m), with an inner loop over i in range(n).
Print each result row with ' '.join(str(x) for x in row).

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and M (the number of rows and columns).
Next N lines: the M integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: M lines: the rows of the transposed matrix, each with N integers separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Flatten 2D Matrix
questions.objective: Flatten an N x M matrix into a 1D list in row-major order.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read an N x M matrix and print all its items as one flat list.
• Use row-major order: first all items of row 0 from left to right, then all items of row 1, and so on
• Store the items in a new 1D list first, then print it
• Do not use sum(matrix, []), itertools or any library; use loops

Example: for the 3 x 2 matrix
1 2
3 4
5 6
the output is 1 2 3 4 5 6.

Given a matrix, print the flattened list.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and M (the number of rows and columns).
Next N lines: the M integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: all N x M items in row-major order, separated by single spaces.
hints: Start with an empty result list.
Use two nested loops: for row in matrix, then for x in row.
Append each x to the result (or use result.extend(row) for each row), then print it joined with spaces.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and M (the number of rows and columns).
Next N lines: the M integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: all N x M items in row-major order, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Matrix Multiplication
questions.objective: Compute matrix product of N x K matrix and K x M matrix.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read an N x K matrix a and a K x M matrix b, and print their product c, which is an N x M matrix.
• Each item c[i][j] is the sum of a[i][t] * b[t][j] for every t from 0 to K - 1. In words: multiply row i of a by column j of b, item by item, and add the products
• Do not use numpy or any library

Example: for a =
1 2
3 4
and b =
5 6
7 8
the output is
19 22
43 50
because c[0][0] = 1*5 + 2*7 = 19.

Given a and b, print the product matrix.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: three integers N, K and M.
Next N lines: the K integers of one row of a.
Next K lines: the M integers of one row of b.
questions.output_format: N lines: the rows of the product matrix, each with M integers separated by single spaces.
hints: Read N rows into a, then K rows into b, with a list comprehension for each row.
Create the result first as N rows of M zeros: [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]. Do not use [[0] * m] * n, which shares one row.
Use three nested loops over i, j and t, and add a[i][t] * b[t][j] to c[i][j].

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: three integers N, K and M.
Next N lines: the K integers of one row of a.
Next K lines: the M integers of one row of b.
extra_fields.output_format: N lines: the rows of the product matrix, each with M integers separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Pascal's Triangle Generator
questions.objective: Generate first N rows of Pascal's triangle returned as list of lists.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: In Pascal's triangle every row starts and ends with 1, and every other number is the sum of the two numbers just above it.

Row 0: 1
Row 1: 1 1
Row 2: 1 2 1
Row 3: 1 3 3 1

Read n, build the first n rows of Pascal's triangle as a list of lists, and print them.
• Row r has r + 1 numbers
• Inside a row, the item at position j (not the first or last) equals prev[j - 1] + prev[j], where prev is the row before
• Print each row on its own line, numbers separated by spaces

Example: for n = 4 the output is
1
1 1
1 2 1
1 3 3 1

Given n, print the first n rows.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the integer n.
questions.output_format: n lines: row r has r + 1 integers separated by single spaces.
hints: Start with triangle = [] and build one row at a time in a loop over r in range(n).
Each new row begins as [1] * (r + 1).
For j from 1 to r - 1, set row[j] = triangle[r - 1][j - 1] + triangle[r - 1][j].

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the integer n.
extra_fields.output_format: n lines: row r has r + 1 integers separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes Array
questions.objective: Generate list of all primes up to N using a boolean sieve array.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A prime is a whole number greater than 1 whose only divisors are 1 and itself. The Sieve of Eratosthenes finds all primes up to n with a list of True/False values.

Read n and print all primes from 2 to n (including n if it is prime), in increasing order.
• Make a list is_prime of n + 1 values, all True at first. Then set is_prime[0] and is_prime[1] to False
• For each number p starting from 2 while p * p <= n: if is_prime[p] is still True, mark every multiple p*p, p*p + p, p*p + 2p, ... up to n as False
• At the end, every index that is still True is a prime

Example: for n = 20 the output is 2 3 5 7 11 13 17 19.

Given n, print the primes up to n.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the integer n.
questions.output_format: One line: all primes <= n in increasing order, separated by single spaces.
hints: Create the list with is_prime = [True] * (n + 1).
Start crossing out at p * p: smaller multiples were already crossed out by smaller primes.
range(p * p, n + 1, p) gives exactly the multiples to mark as False.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())

is_prime = [True] * (n + 1)
is_prime[0] = False
is_prime[1] = False

p = 2
while p * p <= n:
    if is_prime[p]:
        for multiple in range(p * p, n + 1, p):
            is_prime[multiple] = False
    p += 1

primes = [i for i in range(n + 1) if is_prime[i]]
print(" ".join(str(x) for x in primes))

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the integer n.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: all primes <= n in increasing order, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Longest Common Prefix
questions.objective: Find the longest common prefix among a list of strings.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A prefix is a part at the start of a string. For example fl is a prefix of flower.

Read a list of words and print the longest string that is a prefix of EVERY word.
• If the words have no common prefix, print NONE
• If there is only one word, the answer is that word
• Upper and lower case are different: A and a do not match

Examples: for flower flow flight the output is fl. For dog car the output is NONE.

Given the words, print their longest common prefix.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the words, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: the longest common prefix, or NONE if it is empty.
questions.constraints:
1 <= number of words <= 200
1 <= length of each word <= 200
Words contain no spaces
hints: Split the line into a list with input().split(). The prefix can never be longer than the shortest word.
Check position i = 0, 1, 2, ... and compare the character words[0][i] with the same position in every other word.
As soon as one word is too short or has a different character, the prefix is words[0][:i]: stop both loops.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the words, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: the longest common prefix, or NONE if it is empty.

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.objective: Merge two already-sorted integer lists into single sorted list in O(N+M).
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read two lists of integers that are already sorted in increasing order, merge them into one sorted list, and print it.
• Do not use sorted() or list.sort(): that would be slower than needed
• Use two positions, one in each list. Each step, take the smaller of the two current items and move that position forward
• When one list runs out, add all the remaining items of the other list
• Keep duplicates: if a value appears in both lists, it appears twice in the result

Example: for the lists 1 3 5 and 2 3 6 the output is 1 2 3 3 5 6.

Given the two sorted lists, print the merged list.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the first sorted list, integers separated by single spaces.
Line 2: the second sorted list, integers separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: all items of both lists in increasing order, separated by single spaces.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of each list <= 10^5
-10^9 <= each value <= 10^9
Both lists are sorted in increasing order
hints: Start with i = 0, j = 0 and an empty result list.
While i < len(l1) and j < len(l2), append the smaller of l1[i] and l2[j] and move that index forward.
After the loop, add what is left with result.extend(l1[i:]) and result.extend(l2[j:]).
questions.reference_solution:
l1 = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
l2 = [int(x) for x in input().split()]

i = 0
j = 0
result = []

while i < len(l1) and j < len(l2):
    if l1[i] <= l2[j]:
        result.append(l1[i])
        i += 1
    else:
        result.append(l2[j])
        j += 1

# One list is finished; copy the rest of the other one
result.extend(l1[i:])
result.extend(l2[j:])

print(" ".join(str(x) for x in result))

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: the first sorted list, integers separated by single spaces.
Line 2: the second sorted list, integers separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: all items of both lists in increasing order, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Spiral Matrix Traversal Order
questions.objective: Print all elements of N x M matrix in spiral traversal order.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read an N x M matrix and print all its items in spiral order.

Spiral order starts at the top-left corner and goes clockwise around the outside of the matrix, then continues inward:
• Go right along the top row
• Go down the right column
• Go left along the bottom row
• Go up the left column
• Repeat on the smaller matrix inside, until every item has been visited exactly once

Be careful with matrices that have a single row or a single column: no item may be visited twice.

Example: for the 3 x 3 matrix
1 2 3
4 5 6
7 8 9
the output is 1 2 3 6 9 8 7 4 5.

Given a matrix, print its items in spiral order.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and M (the number of rows and columns).
Next N lines: the M integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One line: all N x M items in spiral order, separated by single spaces.
hints: Keep four borders: top, bottom, left and right. Start with top = 0, bottom = N - 1, left = 0, right = M - 1.
After walking the top row, do top += 1. After the right column, right -= 1, and so on for the other two sides.
Before walking the bottom row check top <= bottom, and before walking the left column check left <= right. This stops double visits.
questions.reference_solution:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
matrix = []
for _ in range(n):
    matrix.append([int(x) for x in input().split()])

result = []
top = 0
bottom = n - 1
left = 0
right = m - 1

while top <= bottom and left <= right:
    for j in range(left, right + 1):          # top row, left to right
        result.append(matrix[top][j])
    top += 1

    for i in range(top, bottom + 1):          # right column, downward
        result.append(matrix[i][right])
    right -= 1

    if top <= bottom:
        for j in range(right, left - 1, -1):  # bottom row, right to left
            result.append(matrix[bottom][j])
        bottom -= 1

    if left <= right:
        for i in range(bottom, top - 1, -1):  # left column, upward
            result.append(matrix[i][left])
        left += 1

print(" ".join(str(x) for x in result))

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and M (the number of rows and columns).
Next N lines: the M integers of one row, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: all N x M items in spiral order, separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Generate N x N Spiral Matrix
questions.objective: Generate N x N matrix populated with 1 to N^2 in spiral order.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Read n and build an n x n matrix filled with the numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., n*n in spiral order, then print it.

Spiral order starts at the top-left corner and goes clockwise:
• Fill the top row from left to right
• Fill the right column from top to bottom
• Fill the bottom row from right to left
• Fill the left column from bottom to top
• Repeat on the smaller square inside until all n*n places are filled

Create the matrix as n separate rows (do not use [[0] * n] * n, which makes every row the same list).

Example: for n = 3 the output is
1 2 3
8 9 4
7 6 5

Given n, print the spiral matrix.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the integer n.
questions.output_format: n lines: the rows of the matrix, each with n integers separated by single spaces.
hints: Start with grid = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)] and a counter num = 1.
Use four borders top, bottom, left and right, exactly like a spiral traversal, but write num into each place instead of reading it.
Add 1 to num after every write and move the borders inward after each side.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the integer n.
extra_fields.output_format: n lines: the rows of the matrix, each with n integers separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Trapping Rain Water Array
questions.objective: Compute trapped rainwater given list of elevation heights.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Imagine a row of bars, each of width 1. The height of bar i is heights[i]. After it rains, water is trapped in the dips between the bars.

Read the heights and print the total amount of trapped water.
• The water above bar i reaches the level min(highest bar on its left, highest bar on its right), including bar i itself
• So the water above bar i is min(max_left, max_right) - heights[i], which is never negative
• Water can flow off both ends of the row, so the first and last bars never hold water
• Aim for O(N) time and O(1) extra space

Example: for the heights 0 1 0 2 1 0 1 3 2 1 2 1 the output is 6.

Given the heights, print the trapped water.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the heights, separated by single spaces.
questions.output_format: One integer: the total units of trapped water.
hints: A simple O(N) solution builds two lists: the highest bar up to each position from the left, and from the right.
To use O(1) space, use two pointers left and right moving toward each other, plus left_max and right_max.
Move the side with the smaller current height: its water level is decided by its own max, because the other side is at least as tall.
questions.reference_solution:
heights = [int(x) for x in input().split()]

left = 0
right = len(heights) - 1
left_max = 0
right_max = 0
water = 0

while left < right:
    if heights[left] < heights[right]:
        # The right side is taller, so left_max limits the water here
        left_max = max(left_max, heights[left])
        water += left_max - heights[left]
        left += 1
    else:
        right_max = max(right_max, heights[right])
        water += right_max - heights[right]
        right -= 1

print(water)

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the heights, separated by single spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: One integer: the total units of trapped water.
